title: Prove shared TypeScript terminal UI in WebView2 and VS Code
commit_note: The supplied workspace is not a Git checkout; authority, baseline archive, source manifest, dispatch, scenario, fixture, and delivery hashes are used as immutable references.
changed_paths: ui/packages/*/dist/ and vscode/square-vscode/dist/ (generated build output removed from delivery)
implementation_summary: Added one canonical eight-terminal state fixture, canonical semantic hash, benchmark manifest, scenario manifest, strict bridge catalogue, evidence schema, dispatch packet, and complete task-local source hash manifest.

Implemented one shared TypeScript workspace and xterm.js adapter used unchanged by WPF/WebView2 and VS Code webview hosts, with Operations, Focus Agent, Plan, Review, and Resources presentation presets.

Implemented a bounded sequence-preserving terminal presentation queue with explicit duplicate, gap, and overflow outcomes, animation-frame visible writes, slower hidden-pane writes, and catch-up without sequence loss.

Implemented deterministic ANSI/Unicode high-volume fixture output and a 27-cell one/four/eight-terminal by theme by scale benchmark with duration, byte, batch, sequence, accessibility, and available memory evidence.
Implemented controller-mode input gating, resize messages, keyboard focus movement, unique accessible terminal/output/controller labels, xterm screen-reader mode, and textual controller indicators.

Implemented strict unknown-type/unknown-field bridge parsing in TypeScript and C#, a nonce/local-only VS Code CSP, WebView2 local virtual-origin/navigation restrictions, and no arbitrary shell-command bridge operation.

Added a fail-closed Windows runner that verifies pinned toolchains and source identities, launches both hosts with isolated user-data directories, compares semantic evidence, and marks manual host evidence diagnostic only.
Removed generated production UI/extension dist artifacts that were present in the delivered SP00-T03 archive; no production source was removed.
